families.why: unrolled_k is the only family I control that has produced feasible points (40 feasible, best luts_plus_ffs 415, 15/19 on the merged front). The spec needs >=1 MSPS throughput and <=2^-10 error. unrolled_k with k=2..4 gives ceil(N/k)+3 cycles/result; with N~10-14 and k=2-4 that is ~5-10 cycles/result, so Fmax must be >=100-200 MHz to hit 1 MSPS. Narrowing data_width to 12-16 and n_iter to 10-14 focuses on the accuracy/area sweet spot: W=12 gives output LSB 2^-10, so n_iter must be high enough that CORDIC residual error stays below 2^-10. angle_guard -2..0 and frac_guard 0..1 keep the datapath narrow to minimize LUTs+FFs while still meeting the error bound. k=2..4 balances throughput (need enough rotations/cycle) against area (more parallel shift/add chains). This is where the trade-off curve lives for my assigned families.

iterative produced 0 feasible points in 33 evals, likely because its N+3 cycle latency (N~10-14 means 13-17 cycles/result) requires Fmax >= 130-170 MHz for 1 MSPS, and the shared datapath may not reach that Fmax at the widths needed for 2^-10 accuracy. However, iterative has the smallest area per rotation (single datapath, no k-way parallelism), so if it can meet throughput at all, it could dominate on luts_plus_ffs. I keep a small share to probe whether any iterative config clears the throughput constraint at the minimal area, which would expand the Pareto front toward the low-area end. If it remains infeasible, the budget is cheap insurance.

parsed.rationale: The fleet facts show unrolled_k is my workhorse: 40 feasible points, best area 415, and 15 of 19 merged-front designs. iterative has been infeasible so far (0/33), likely a throughput wall. The spec's binding constraints are throughput >=1 MSPS and max_abs_err <= 2^-10. For unrolled_k, the key trade-off is k (throughput vs area) and n_iter/data_width (accuracy vs area). I focus 70% of budget on unrolled_k with tight ranges around the known-feasible region (W 12-16, N 10-14, k 2-4, minimal guards) to densely map the Pareto front in the area/accuracy space. The remaining 30% probes iterative at the same accuracy settings to check if any low-area point sneaks through the throughput constraint, which would extend the front to lower luts_plus_ffs. Both families compute identical bits, so accuracy tuning is shared; the difference is purely in the datapath structure and resulting Fmax/area.
